translation.text:
<meta>Page 447 of a red xylographic blockprint edition of the Mongolian Kanjur or Dandjur. Only the bilingual Mongolian and Chinese marginal folio markers are transcribed in the OCR; the thirty-one vertical lines of the main body text were not transcribed.</meta>
<warning>Traditional vertical Mongolian (Uighur-Mongolian) script in red xylographic blockprint (Peking Kanjur / Dandjur format) with Chinese and Mongolian marginal volume/folio markers; main body text consists of 31 vertical lines of classical Mongolian Buddhist scripture that cannot be reliably transcribed line-by-line into Unicode/Latin without character-level errors.</warning>
<margin>11, Upper part: Having Reached the Other Shore of the Secret <note>original: "᠑᠑ ᠦᠨ ᠠ ᠨᠢᠭᠤᠴᠠ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ ᠬᠢᠵᠠᠭᠠᠷ ᠠ ᠬᠦᠷᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ"; a Mongolian marginal title and volume marker for Volume 11, first section, of the Tantra or Secret Perfection section of the Kanjur</note></margin>
<margin>Secret Sutra, Volume 11, Upper Part, Folio 224 <note>original: "祕密經第十一卷上二百二十四"; Chinese blockprint folio marker corresponding to the Mongolian marginal title</note></margin>

<unclear>31 vertical lines of classical Mongolian blockprint text in red ink, not transcribed</unclear>

<summary>This folio from Volume 11 (Upper Part, Folio 224) of the Secret Sutra section of the Peking Mongolian Kanjur features bilingual Mongolian and Chinese marginal markers. The thirty-one vertical lines of classical Mongolian scripture in red blockprint are not transcribed in the source OCR.</summary>
<keywords>Mongolian Kanjur, Secret Sutra, Tantra, Peking blockprint, xylograph, Buddhist scripture, bilingual marginalia, Uighur-Mongolian script</keywords>
